documents.title: AI Guidelines - ChatGPT Edu for Fresno State
documents.stance_why: The page sets no default rule for coursework; it says "Each course may have its own rules and expectations regarding AI usage, set by the instructor" and "When permitted by your instructor", leaving the decision to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: Technology Services page introducing ChatGPT Edu at Fresno State, setting out campus-wide principles and separate guidance for faculty/staff and students. It mostly delegates AI-use decisions to course instructors while requiring citation, disclosure, verification and data protection, and it explains the CSU data-protection and governance arrangements.

documents.title: Student Terms and Conditions for Use of Generative AI Tools & Solutions
documents.stance_why: Course rules vary ("Expectations ... may differ between courses and instructors"), yet there is a baseline that "Submission of fully AI-generated content is prohibited unless explicitly allowed by the faculty member". The baseline leaves the call to faculty rather than banning AI outright, and most other items are conduct duties, so the document delegates to instructors.
documents.summary: Click-through terms that Fresno State students accept before using GenAI tools for academic work. They tie AI use to the cheating and plagiarism policy, bar fully AI-generated submissions unless faculty allow it, require verification, citation and privacy care, and leave course-specific rules to instructors.

documents.stance_why: The guidelines say "faculty make the ﬁnal decisions regarding the use of AI in their courses" and that students "must always consult their instructors", so the course decision is handed to instructors even though CSU "encourages students and faculty to explore AI thoughtfully"; delegates.
documents.summary: CSU system student guidelines, republished by Fresno State Student Affairs, that welcome thoughtful AI exploration while telling students that faculty make the final decision in each course. They set principles on ethical use, integrity, transparency, accountability, fairness and privacy, and ask students to cite AI content and check outputs for bias.
